transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is that my sleep has just gotten really, really messed up. Like, I’ll stay up half the night with my mind just running and running. 

Which is actually how I ended up reorganizing my entire kitchen pantry last week. I bought all these little clear bins online... they were on sale, actually, like 40% off, which is such a good deal because usually those acrylic organizers are way too expensive. I look at spreadsheets all day for my bookkeeping job, so I guess I just like things perfectly categorized, you know? I even printed little labels for the flour and sugar. 

But yeah, I was up doing that at 3 AM because my brain just wouldn't shut off. And then other times, if I don't do that, I'll just wake up way too early and feel like I never even rested at all.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually upbeat, energized, or irritable — like you didn’t need much sleep, were doing a lot of things at once, or felt like you could take on the world?

Well, yeah, actually. Like earlier this month, I felt... I don't know, almost lit up? Like I was just completely unstoppable and could do anything. I was getting so much done. But then, it's weird, because I'd also just snap out of nowhere. Like my mom asked me this totally normal question about what I wanted for dinner, and I just bit her head off. And she makes this really good chicken parm, by the way, with the homemade sauce that takes like four hours to simmer. She got the recipe from my grandmother who came over from Italy, well, not Italy, but her parents did. Anyway, I also snapped at my supervisor at work over something so stupid. She just asked me to double-check a ledger, which is literally my job, but I got so incredibly irritated. I usually never act like that. I'm usually the one who brings donuts in on Fridays, you know? The ones from that bakery down on 4th street with the pink boxes. They have the best apple fritters. But yeah, I just felt so energized but also so on edge at the same time.
Can you tell me more about that time you felt so energized and on edge? How long did that feeling last?

Um, let's see... I'd say that whole thing, where I was super charged up and then just completely crashed, that's been happening for about a month now. It started right around the time my mortgage payments started feeling really, really real. Which is terrifying, honestly. I mean, buying a house at 26 sounds great until you actually have to pay for it every month. It’s this cute little two-bedroom, though. It has this original hardwood flooring from like the 1950s that I’ve been trying to restore. I watched like ten hours of YouTube tutorials on sanding and refinishing, and I bought this special polyurethane coat that’s supposed to be eco-friendly. The guy at the hardware store said it takes forever to dry, but it's better for you. He was super helpful, actually, his name was Dave. He had this really funny accent, maybe from Boston? I've always wanted to visit Boston. But anyway, yeah, about a month of this back and forth stuff since the house stuff got so stressful.
After that month of feeling energized and on edge, did you experience a period where you felt very down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, actually... it’s like the complete opposite of all that energy. Lately, I just wake up with this really heavy, empty feeling. It’s so weird because I’ll just be sitting in my own condo, the place I worked so incredibly hard to get, and it just makes me want to cry. 

And I don’t even know why. I was just sitting on my couch the other day crying—it’s this really cute mid-century modern one I found on Wayfair. I actually had a promo code for free shipping, which is huge because freight shipping is usually a total rip-off. I always check the shipping costs on the invoices at work, and you wouldn't believe what some of these logistics companies charge us. It’s practically extortion. My friend Sarah ordered a dining table once and it got lost in transit for like a month, and she had to eat off a cardboard box. She has this cat, Barnaby, who kept trying to chew on the box... he's an orange tabby, super cute but he really menaces her houseplants. She had to buy all fake ones. 

But um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. Yeah, I just sit on that couch and feel totally hopeless, like I don't even care about doing anything I usually enjoy anymore.

During the time you felt so energized and on edge, was there a period where you felt unusually high, like your mood was abnormally upbeat or irritable for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least four days in a row?

Yeah, exactly like I was saying before. Earlier in the month, I just felt almost lit up and totally unstoppable, and it definitely lasted for at least four days in a row, probably more. I'd wake up just buzzing, but then I’d snap at my mom or my supervisor over these little questions that normally wouldn’t bother me at all. 

I think it started on a Tuesday, because Tuesday is when we do the weekly bank reconciliations at work. I have this dual-monitor setup at my desk, which you really need for bookkeeping, otherwise you're just constantly tabbing back and forth between windows and it drives you crazy. My left monitor actually has a dead pixel right in the middle, so I put a tiny little piece of a sticky note over it so I'd stop staring at it. Post-its are getting so expensive, by the way. Our office manager switched us to this cheap off-brand kind and they don't even stick to the plastic monitor bezels. They just curl up and fall right onto my keyboard. It's so annoying when you're trying to use the 10-key pad. I'm actually really fast at 10-key, I learned it back in high school and it's basically muscle memory now. 

But um, yeah, for like a solid week or so I was just super upbeat and going a million miles an hour all day, but also just so irritable if anyone got in my way.
During that time when you felt so energized and irritable, did you also feel like your mood was unusually high or even euphoric for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a full week?

Yeah, I think that's what I was trying to explain just a minute ago. Like, earlier in the month, I felt almost lit up, you know? Just completely unstoppable and on top of the world. But then, almost in the same breath, I’d snap at my mom or my supervisor over these tiny little questions that normally wouldn’t bother me at all. 

It was so intense, and it definitely lasted for a whole week, maybe even a little longer. I remember because I had to go to my mom's house that weekend for a family barbecue. She makes this incredible potato salad, she puts a little bit of dill pickle relish in it, which sounds weird but it totally works. My aunt Cheryl always tries to bring her own potato salad to compete, and hers is just awful. It's so bland, like she doesn't even know what salt is. Cheryl is actually my dad's sister, and they have this really weird dynamic where they're always trying to one-up each other. Like last Christmas, my dad bought my grandma this huge flat-screen TV, and then Cheryl went out and bought her a subscription to every streaming service under the sun. My grandma doesn't even know how to use a smart TV, she still has a VCR hooked up to her old set. I had to go over there and program the remote for her, which took like three hours because the manual was printed in the tiniest font imaginable. I swear they do that on purpose so you have to call their customer service line. 

But um, yeah, what were we talking about? Oh, right. The mood thing. Yeah, it was a solid week of feeling like a superhero but also wanting to bite everyone's head off.

During that week when you felt like a superhero and were full of energy, did you also notice that you needed much less sleep than usual, talked more than you normally do, or felt like your thoughts were racing?

Yeah, the sleep thing was crazy. There were several nights where I only slept like three or four hours, but I’d still get up feeling totally charged, like I didn't even need coffee. Which is huge for me, because normally I am a total zombie without my morning latte. I usually go to this little coffee shop down the street from my condo, they have this amazing lavender syrup they make in-house. It’s so much better than the stuff they use at the big chain places, which just tastes like soap, honestly. I tried making my own lavender syrup once because I thought it would save money, you know, being a bookkeeper I'm always looking at my own personal budget too. But I bought the wrong kind of lavender, apparently there's culinary lavender and then there's the kind you put in sachets for your drawers? I accidentally used the drawer kind and my kitchen smelled like a grandma's closet for a week. My mom thought it was hilarious. She’s always making fun of my DIY projects because they never turn out right. Like the time I tried to re-upholster a dining chair and ended up stapling my own shirt to the seat cushion. I had to walk around with a chair attached to me until my neighbor came over with pliers. 

But um, wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, sleep and talking and stuff. Yeah, I didn't need much sleep at all, and I was definitely talking a lot more than usual. My thoughts were just zooming.
